title: Path traversal review for file access
when: An app reads, writes, serves, downloads or extracts files using names from URLs, form fields, archives or uploads, and path traversal must be ruled out.
prompt:
Goal: Every file access built from outside input provably stays inside its root, after decoding, normalizing and following links.
Steps:
1. Find sinks: fs.readFile, createReadStream, writeFile, unlink, rename, file send helpers, open() in Python, archive extraction loops.
2. Decode once first (decodeURIComponent inside try), refuse names containing \0, then const full = path.resolve(root, name).
3. Accept only full === root or full.startsWith(root + path.sep), with root itself resolved; on case insensitive disks lowercase both first.
4. Follow links: const real = await fs.realpath(full) and repeat the prefix check, so a symlink inside root cannot point outside.
5. Zip slip: run every archive entry name through the same check before writing; refuse absolute paths, drive letters such as C: and backslashes on win32.
6. Best fix when possible: never use names as paths; look files up by id and store them under generated names.
Quality bar:
- One shared safeJoin(root, name) serves every sink.
- Tests: ../../etc/passwd, ..%2f..%2f, ....//, /etc/passwd, C:\temp\x and a symlink leading out.
- Errors reply 404 without echoing the resolved path.
Pitfalls:
- Checking for ".." before decoding.
- startsWith(root) without the separator, so /data2 passes for /data.
- path.join, which walks out of the root happily.
Verify:
- [ ] Every sink uses safeJoin.
- [ ] The realpath check exists.
- [ ] Archive entries are checked.
- [ ] Payload tests get 404.
Output: Findings in SECURITY-AUDIT.md, safe-path.mjs and test/safe-path.test.mjs.

examples.input: a rota de download recebe ?file= e le do disco
examples.output: safeJoin with resolve plus separator check, realpath recheck, zip entry check, payload tests
